title: The rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties
gap_note: Full, direct (the only step is that the Lean CM hypothesis is an equivalent cohomological reformulation of the paper's CM). Challenge.lean:38-43 is, for every X over Spec C that is integral, smooth, projective and carries GrpObj X (an abelian variety), with HasComplexMultiplication X and every p : N, Hdg^p(X;Q) <= algebraicCycleClassSpan X p. Hdg^p = classes of H^{2p}(X(C);Q) (Mathlib sheaf cohomology of the constant sheaf Q on the analytic space X(C)) whose image in holomorphic de Rham H_dR^{2p} lies in F^p ⊓ conj(F^p), the standard (p,p) rational classes; algebraicCycleClassSpan X p = Q-span of the fundamental classes [Z] of all integral closed subvarieties Z of codimension p (generic points x with Order.coheight x = p, which Mathlib uses for codimension; [Z] built from supported cohomology H^{2p}_Z, purity on Z_reg and an explicit complex-orientation normalisation, then forget support). That is exactly the paper's Theorem 1.1 for all p and all dimensions (the 0-dimensional case is allowed: factors = 0). The conclusion is the literal conclusion of the upstream HodgeConjectureForAbelianVarieties (HodgeConjecture/Variants.lean:66-69); the only addition is hCM. Hypothesis match: paper CM = End(A)⊗Q contains a commutative semisimple Q-algebra of dimension 2 dim A (01-introduction.tex:10-14). Lean CM (CM.lean:38-58) = Q-linear iso H^1(X;Q) ≅ ∏_{i<n} K_i with every K_i a CM number field (fields may repeat or differ), such that ∏K_i, acting on H^1 through that iso, preserves F^1 H_dR^1 under the Q-linear comparison C⊗H^1 -> H_dR^1; i.e. a free rank-one action of a 2g-dimensional commutative semisimple algebra by Hodge endomorphisms. Lean-CM implies paper-CM via End^0(A)=End_HS(H^1(A,Q)); paper-CM implies Lean-CM by A ~ ∏B_j^{n_j} with B_j simple CM, End^0(B_j) a CM field of degree 2 dim B_j and H^1(B_j,Q) one-dimensional over it (take K_j repeated n_j times). The two are equivalent by classical theory not proved in Lean, so the Lean hypothesis is not literally the paper's. Not in Lean (outside the selected statement per lean/docs/032.md and the summary's 'Through Milne's theorems, this also gives'): the Tate conjecture over finite fields, the Hodge standard conjecture (paper Corollaries at 07-consequences.tex:213 and :274, deduced from Theorem 1.1 plus Milne's external theorems) and the generalized Hodge conjecture (07-consequences.tex:154, not in the summary). Applications of this kind do not make the verdict partial under the rubric.
suspicious_defs: ComparatorChallenges/HodgeConjectureCMAbelianVarieties/CM.lean:25-58 diagonalAction/h1Comparison/CMH1Data/HasComplexMultiplication: hand-built cohomological CM notion (not End^0); requires CM-field factors and F^1 preservation only (conjugate filtration follows since the action is rational). h1Comparison is only Q-linear. Equivalent to the paper's CM but with extra content (see gap_note).

HodgeConjecture/Definitions/AlgebraicGeometry/Hodge/Filtration.lean:819-822,839-845,934-962: F^p H_dR^n := image of hypercohomology of the stupid truncation sigma_{>=p} of the holomorphic de Rham complex; conjugation is transported through H^n(X(C);C) ≅ H_dR^n; hodgeClasses K X p := preimage under the K-coefficient comparison of F^p ⊓ conj F^p. Standard definition, nonstandard packaging (Mathlib derived-category Hom, SmallShiftedHom).

HodgeConjecture/Definitions/AlgebraicGeometry/Hodge/HolomorphicDeRham.lean:62-123: holomorphic p-forms defined as Kahler forms of the algebra of holomorphic functions modulo the chart-evaluation kernel, sheafified; the holomorphic Poincare quasi-isomorphism C[0] -> Omega^. is proved (lines 528, 612-621), so the complex is not degenerate.

HodgeConjecture/Definitions/AlgebraicGeometry/Cycle/FundamentalClass.lean:136-159: algebraicCycleClassSpan = sSup over points x with Order.coheight x = p of span{cycleComponentSheafClass}; classes constructed in H^{2p}_{Z(C)}(X(C);Q) by gluing normalised local coclasses on Z_reg (Cycle/Component/SmoothSupportCoclassSection.lean), unique extension across Z_sing, forgetSupport. Orientation normalisation uses an explicit simplex (LocalHomology/FundamentalClass.lean, ComplexClass.lean). Non-textbook construction, not audited line by line; only its span matters.

title: Local smoothing for the Euclidean wave equation
gap_note: Full, direct. euclidean_local_smoothing (LocalSmoothing.lean:84-96) is Theorem 1.1 of the Oct-25 paper (introduction.tex:16-23): all n>=2, all real p>=2, eps>0 or (p=2, eps=0), Sobolev order max(0,(n-1)/2-n/p)+eps, half wave with symbol e^{-it|xi|} on Schwartz data over Lebesgue measure on R^n x [1,2], W^{s,p} norm = L^p norm of the Bessel potential (1+|xi|^2)^{s/2}, C=C(n,p,eps) chosen before f; it adds that both sides are finite. Only routine remarks are left to the reader: density beyond Schwartz data and conjugation for the e^{+it|D|} sign (both stated in introduction.tex:31-34). The Sept-24 paper's critical L^3 result in n=3 (00-introduction.tex:25-32) is the instance n=3, p=3. Rest of the summary = consequences ('The wave estimate yields', 'It also gives', 'follow', 'In particular'; the paper's own heading is 'Consequences for Fourier analysis and geometry'), so by the rubric they do not make the verdict partial. Coverage of each: bochner_riesz = Bochner-Riesz conjecture, uniform in R, 1<=p<=infinity, delta>max(n|1/p-1/2|-1/2,0) (consequences.tex:16-23, eq. br-uniform); stein_square = Stein square function (stein_square.tex:21-28, the literal r d/dr form, 2<=p<infinity, alpha>max(1/2,n(1/2-1/p))); spherical_restriction = sphere extension L^a->L^b, 1<a<=infinity, b>2n/(n-1), b>(n+1)/(n-1)a' (global-extension.tex:13-27); kakeya_maximal = Kakeya maximal conjecture, L^n(R^n)->L^n(S^{n-1}) with delta^{-eps} loss (paper proves the stronger log(2/delta)^{4/p_c}, kakeya.tex:14-23); kakeya = Hausdorff dimension n for every set (no measurability) containing a unit segment in each direction. NO challenge statement for: maximal bounds for the Bochner-Riesz means B_*^alpha, 2<=p<infinity (consequences.tex:25-29) and the a.e./norm convergence; restriction for the compact paraboloid and the truncated cone (global-extension.tex:22-23; parabolic.tex:20-25); local smoothing for the Schroedinger equation (parabolic.tex:26-38); the Nikodym maximal estimate (kakeya.tex:264-270). The scope note's dimension-3 tube-volume lower bound is also outside the challenge (and the summary).

title: Disproof of the Exponential Time Hypothesis
gap_note: Full; the Lean states the algorithmic claim directly, up to routine bookkeeping. For each k>=2 it gives ONE fixed deterministic multi-tape Turing machine (chosen after k, before n and F) that on the canonical encoding of any width<=k CNF over Fin n halts after `time` steps with the exact count in little-endian binary on countTape, the bit [0<count] on answerTape and as the halting answer, with time <= C (L+1)^d 2^{A n (ln ln(n+16))^2/sqrt(ln(n+16))} (L = bit length of the encoding) and every execution prefix visiting <= S (L+1)^e cells (space: not in the headline, so the Lean is stronger there). Routine steps to the summary: (i) polynomial equivalence of L and n+m: L >= n+4m+2 and L <= n+2+4m+2km(4n+2), so (L+1)^d = (n+m)^{O_k(1)}; (ii) exponent: A*n(lnln n)^2/sqrt(ln n) = n/(ln n)^{1/2+o(1)} with o(1) -> 0 from below; the paper identifies rho(n)=n(loglog n)^2/sqrt(log n)=n/(log n)^{1/2+o(1)} itself (main_full_version.tex:87-92) and its abstract (lines 30-39) states exactly the summary's bound; (iii) inputs with duplicate or unsorted clauses are canonicalised in poly time (the Lean input is a Finset of Finsets, encoded sorted). Exponent comparison: the Lean exponent is the paper's weaker rho(n) bound obtained by rational interpolation, not Theorem 1.1's 2^{O_k(n loglog n/sqrt(log n))} and not the sparse (m<=Dn) 2^{O(n/sqrt(log n))}; neither refinement is in the summary or the Lean. No n>=20 restriction in the Lean (the +16 shift covers small n). ETH: with k=3 (hk: 2<=3), distinct 3-clauses over Fin n number O(n^3), so L=O(n^4) and 3-SAT is decided by a TM in n^{O(1)} 2^{o(n)} time, contradicting 2^{Omega(n)}; ETH itself is not defined in Lean, so the refutation is the evident reading of the algorithm, not a formal statement. Not in Lean: the E^NP circuit lower bound (paper Cor. cor:quantitative-circuits, main_full_version.tex:183-190, via Williams and the fixed-density case); it is introduced by 'This yields', a corollary, so by the rubric it does not make the verdict partial.
suspicious_defs: ComparatorChallenges/SubexponentialSAT.lean:55-81 Encoding.encodeNat/frame/encodeList/encodeCNF: hand-built canonical encoding; n and every literal code (2*var+sign) are written in UNARY and each bit is doubled by `frame`, so L = Theta(k n m) rather than O(m log n); bit length enters only through (L+1)^d, which is polynomially equivalent to (n+m)^{O(1)}.

SubexponentialSAT.lean:92-126 Computation.PrimitiveMachine/step/init/Trace: own multi-tape TM model (Mathlib TM0.Stmt on Option Bool, each state scans ONE tape chosen by `scan` and does one move or write; halting is a transition `inl answer`; the input tape is writable). Standard up to constant factors; Trace counts exactly the successful steps.

SubexponentialSAT.lean:149-189 LocatedCfg/monitor/visitedSpace: ghost head-position/min/max bookkeeping; space = sum over ALL tapes of (upper-lower+1), input tape initialised to input.length (so input counts as space).

SubexponentialSAT.lean:130-141 SqrtLog.Statement.runtimeScale/runtimeBound: time bound constant*(inputBits+1)^degree*2^(exponentConstant*n*(ln ln(n+16))^2/sqrt(ln(n+16))); C, A real and d natural are free (existential, positive), i.e. an asymptotic O_k statement, vacuous for small n if A is huge.
